learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with the main tools of Mathematical Analysis, as well as knowledge of infinitesimal calculus, differentiation, integration, and their applications, regarding both functions of a single variable and functions of several variables.
Acquire the autonomy to use this knowledge as tools for evaluation and interpretation in various fields.
Acquire communication skills characterized by rigor and clarity.

syllabus_topics: Derivatives of the composition of functions
Main integration's methods: decomposition in sum
Main integration's methods: of rational functions
Limits and continuity for several variables
Relative maximum and minimum for several variables
Necessary and sufficient conditions for extrema
Bernoulli's and other types of equations
assessment_rules: The exam consists of two partial written tests and an oral exam. The first partial written test is graded out of thirty and remains valid up to and including the December exam session. The second partial written test is evaluated concurrently with the oral exam, which includes theoretical questions and a discussion of the second written test's exercises. The final grade is based on a weighted average of these evaluations.
